intro: Google Docs voice typing only works inside Google Docs in the browser (Tools > Voice typing). If you want to talk in any Mac app, Lazur dictates everywhere and also answers questions about your screen.
tldr: Google Docs voice typing is a dictation tool. Lazur is a voice assistant that also dictates.
Pick Google Docs voice typing if typing by voice is all you need.
Pick Lazur if you also want help with what is on your screen: answers, pointing at buttons, step-by-step guidance.
Lazur is free for 3 days, then $18/month.

faq.question: Is Lazur a good Google Docs voice typing alternative?
faq.answer: If you want more than dictation, yes. Lazur dictates in any Mac app and also answers questions about your screen, points at buttons and guides you. If you only dictate, Google Docs voice typing is a fine choice.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur and Google Docs voice typing together?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as their shortcuts do not clash. Lazur uses hold fn to dictate and hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask.

faq.question: Does Google voice typing work outside Google Docs?
faq.answer: No. It is a Google Docs feature (and speaker notes in Slides). It works in Chrome, Edge and Safari.
